comment:overrides: express 4.22.2 — the last of the 4.x line — pins qs ~6.15.1, so `npm audit fix` CANNOT move qs: the range forbids it. This override is what does. qs parses req.query on every request here (express 4 defaults the query parser to 'extended'), so a qs advisory is reachable on every route rather than theoretical. The floor is 6.16.1 rather than 6.16.0 because THE FIX BECAME THE PIN: the first two moderates (array-limit bypass via bracket-key comma parsing, and DoS via attacker-controlled isBuffer) were fixed in 6.16.0, and a third advisory then named 6.7.0-6.16.0 inclusive — so the version this override was added to reach is itself vulnerable. A floor must sit ABOVE the whole advisory range, or a lockfile-less install can resolve straight back onto it; CI runs `npm ci` and takes the lockfile, but nothing else here promises to. body-parser needs no override and never did: express's own ~1.20.5 admits the fixed 1.20.9, which is why that one really is a lockfile refresh. Express 5 pins a fixed qs and is the real answer; it is not a change to make inside a security patch. Remove this override when express moves. CLAUDE.md §61 R5, §89.
